reference_sql:
SELECT isoyear(observed_ts) AS iso_year,
       week(observed_ts) AS iso_week,
       COUNT(*) AS checks
FROM competitor_prices
WHERE competitor = 'Bliksem'
  AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-23 00:00:00'
  AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00'
GROUP BY isoyear(observed_ts), week(observed_ts)
alternatives: SELECT EXTRACT(isoyear FROM observed_ts) AS iso_year, EXTRACT(week FROM observed_ts) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS checks FROM competitor_prices WHERE competitor = 'Bliksem' AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-23 00:00:00' AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2

SELECT isoyear(date_trunc('week', observed_ts)) AS iso_year, week(date_trunc('week', observed_ts)) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS checks FROM competitor_prices WHERE competitor = 'Bliksem' AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-23 00:00:00' AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00' GROUP BY date_trunc('week', observed_ts)

other_way.sql: SELECT isoyear(date_trunc('week', observed_ts)) AS iso_year, week(date_trunc('week', observed_ts)) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS checks FROM competitor_prices WHERE competitor = 'Bliksem' AND observed_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-23 00:00:00' AND observed_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00' GROUP BY date_trunc('week', observed_ts)
other_way.tradeoff: Grouping by the Monday from date_trunc('week', ...) gives the same ISO weeks, and you read the labels off that Monday.
